people.role: A founder (980) and head of Chân Kim Các, assaying and refining spirit ores
people.appearance: A lean, grey old man with silver burns on his fingertips, who holds every cup of tea a moment too long, as if weighing it.
people.backstory: Tưởng Bách Luyện was a silver-washer's son at Bạch Ngân, where the Pivot strikes its coin (A224), and worked forty years as a refiner in the Pivot's mint without ever being taught its method. In 980 he and four other assayers of the mint founded Chân Kim Các beside the open scales of Song Kiều (V127), sworn to the Pivot, to assay and refine for anyone who would pay a fair fee. He wrote its rule: a house that weighs for others has no root of its own, and takes its apprentices by the eye, not by the element. He refined the flying sword Dawn Charioteer for the Pivot's head in 1168 from Bạch Ngân silver and Thiên Ngoại iron. The Pivot's master of weights, Đặng Quân Bình (dang_quan_binh), has twice caught the house's copy of the standard weight a hair light, and twice Tưởng weighed it himself and found it true, and said so. He believed it the first time. Since 1198 the house's take has tripled, and he has spent it.
people.wants: To leave the house rich and its name clean, and to be thought honest when he is dead.
people.secret: The second time, in 1194, he found out. His granddaughter Tưởng Ngọc Cân (tuong_ngoc_can) shaves the house weight and swaps a true copy in when anyone tests it. He denied it to the Pivot anyway, and it is the only lie he has told aloud. This spring he sent his grandson Tưởng Tri Chuẩn (tuong_tri_chuan), who tests the weights, to keep the house's counter at Bạch Ngân, fifty-five days off, and he is building a fourth furnace with the good-side money.

people.role: The head's granddaughter and keeper of the scales on the house's side of the square at Song Kiều
people.appearance: A small, quick woman in a miner's blue jacket over a merchant's silk, with a set of brass weights she clicks in her palm.
people.backstory: The head's granddaughter by his son and an Ôn of Song Kiều, the bridge-builders who keep the twin bridges' tolls (A229). She grew up on the square where the Pivot weighs the miners' ore (A219), on her mother's side among the miners and on her father's among the assayers. She has kept the house's scales since 1160. The miners prefer her side of the square, and since 1198 they have paid her for it. The Pivot's scale across the square has weighed almost nothing for two winters. Her grandfather (tuong_bach_luyen) spends what she brings in. The Pivot's assayer Hồng Chuẩn Bình (hong_chuan_binh) argues with her across the square every morning about everything except the weight.
people.wants: The whole square: every basket of Ngọc Hành's ore weighed on her side and paying her fee, and the house after her grandfather.
people.secret: She shaves the house weight a hair light, so that ore weighed on her side comes out heavier than at the Pivot's scale, and since 1198 she has charged the miners a good-side fee to stand in her line. With the Pivot's scale idle, she raises the fee each season, and it now takes back most of what the light weight gives them. Quản Thập Thù swaps the true weight in whenever anyone tests the scale, and she pays him from the fee.

people.role: Furnace master of the house, who refines the ore the house assays
people.appearance: A stooped man with red-rimmed eyes and silver-grey skin from a century of furnace fumes.
people.backstory: A silver-miner's son from Bạch Ngân, like his master Tưởng Bách Luyện (tuong_bach_luyen). He did the hundred refinings of the Dawn Charioteer for the Pivot's heir in 1168 and keeps the house's three furnaces. He has refined Thối Tinh's Thiên Ngoại iron for silver inlay, and it melts like mountain iron in his furnace. He has no true star iron to set beside it, so it is a guess. He told the head, and the head said a refiner does not assay unasked, not even a guess.
people.wants: A true piece of star iron to lay beside Thối Tinh's, and leave to say what he thinks of it aloud.
people.secret: Nights, he is assaying Thối Tinh's iron on the sly: Tiền Phân Vi's knife is his sample, and the blade will come back pitted before the apprentice asks a fourth time.

people.role: The house's go-between with the Ôn clan and its bridge tolls
people.appearance: Handsome and easy, with an Ôn jade at each wrist and a toll-ledger under her arm.
people.backstory: An Ôn of the bridge-keeping clan of Song Kiều (A229), cousin to Tưởng Ngọc Cân (tuong_ngoc_can). She settles which ore pays toll on which bridge, and every miner who stands in her cousin's line crosses the Ôn's north bridge to get there. Her grandfather Ôn Trọng Lương (on_trong_luong) wants a fifth of the good-side fee, or the toll on that bridge doubles. She carries his terms to the house, and she has asked the Pivot's Hồng Chuẩn Bình (hong_chuan_binh) what the Pivot would pay to have the miners back.
people.wants: The Ôn's fifth, and a desk where the coin of both squares passes through her hands.
people.secret: She is writing her own tenth into the doubled bridge toll she will announce at the quarter, and her grandfather Ôn Trọng Lương has not been told of it.

people.role: Inner disciple from the spring of Xuân Thủy Thang, the best eye of her year
people.appearance: Smells faintly of the spring's sulphur; wide dark eyes that never blink during a weighing.
people.backstory: A bath-keeper's daughter from the house's hot spring, she told nine silvers apart with her eyes shut at eleven; Tưởng Bách Luyện (tuong_bach_luyen) took her himself.
